text:
mina: Hi team, starting today . Trying to get dev parity between my M2 Mac (zsh) and a Debian VM. Followed the quickstart but running into: asdf not initializing in one shell, Ruby gems failing with OpenSSL, and our local scripts erroring because REDWOOD_API_KEY isn't set. Any minimal foolproof bootstrap?

devx: welcome! shortest path that worked for me:
1) brew (on mac): /opt/homebrew is the prefix on M1/M2. install openssl@3 and pkg-config.
2) asdf via brew or git clone, then `source` the asdf script in your shell rc. For zsh add: `source $(brew --prefix asdf)/libexec/asdf.sh` and for fish use `source (brew --prefix asdf)/libexec/asdf.fish`.
3) set OpenSSL flags before installing ruby/gems: 
```bash
export LDFLAGS="-L$(brew --prefix openssl@3)/lib"
export CPPFLAGS="-I$(brew --prefix openssl@3)/include"
export PKG_CONFIG_PATH="$(brew --prefix openssl@3)/lib/pkgconfig"
```
4) on Debian/WSL: `sudo apt install -y build-essential libssl-dev zlib1g-dev pkg-config libffi-dev` before asdf/ruby.

mina: thanks. asdf seems to work in zsh but not when i `ssh` into the vm. any tips?

devx: ssh shells are often non-login vs login. make sure your ssh user's rc sources asdf: add the `source` line to ~/.profile or ~/.bashrc (depending on the distro) so interactive ssh sessions get it. Also check `which asdf` and `asdf where` to confirm paths.

mina: got it. about REDWOOD_API_KEY and kubeconfig, what's the local pattern? i don't want to accidentally git-add secrets.

ops: don't commit secrets. our convention: use direnv + a local env file. create `~/.config/redwood/env.local` (gitignored) with plain exports: 
```
export REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk-local-xxxx
export REDWOOD_ENV=dev
export KUBECONFIG=~/.kube/config-redwood
```
Then in each repo `.envrc` call `source_env ~/.config/redwood/env.local`. direnv works on mac+linux and prevents accidental commits. If you need vault-backed creds, we can wire that up.

mina: ssh key question: i generated ed25519, is that fine? and where to add it?

ops: ed25519 is preferred. Add the pubkey to your personal GitHub account, then submit the onboarding access form (pinned in #new-hires) to request org/repo rights. Infra will add you to the internal teams and, if necessary, to deploy-key lists.

mina: dotfiles? i want a minimal starter so i don't copy broken snippets.

devx: we maintain a starter repo: https://github.com/redwood-onboarding/dotfiles-starter. It has asdf init lines, direnv examples, and sample gitconfig. Clone and pick bits you want; don't blindly overwrite your dotfiles. If you prefer a synced company-default, ask infra to add you to the dotfiles group.

infra-bot: Created ticket INF-5409 for mina to receive repo and dev cluster access.

mina: perfect. i'll add the openssl flags, update rc files for asdf on the vm, put secrets in env.local, and try again. will post logs here if anything else fails :thumbsup:
